_doc: Central policy for the AI Control Layer. Single source of truth, hot-reloaded on every request (edit and save, no restart). Invalid edits are rejected and the last good policy stays active. Removing a control or setting enabled=false turns it off. action: block | redact | flag (log only) | approve (human). mode: enforce | monitor (shadow mode: nothing is blocked, everything that would be is logged).

models._doc: Allowed LLMs (llm_complete tool, Ollama proxy). roles: agent = the model the agent talks to (qwen3:4b-instruct via the proxy), guard = used only by the semantic layer. Digests for local models are pinned in controls.semantic.pinned_digests (the proxy refuses a model whose digest changed). Local-only: no paid or remote model is allowed in this committed demo policy (privacy claim). Paid-model support (USD budgets) stays in code; see policy.paid-example.json. Local models are budgeted in compute time.

budgets._doc: Per session (one agent run). Any limit hit = DENY with guardrail 'budget'. max_compute_ms is 120000 in this demo policy (policy.paid-example.json keeps 30000): since F16 prompt checks count local-model time too, and a judges' session of ~25-30 prompts with guard models would hit 30 s. With 120 s, max_calls (40) is the limit a live session reaches first.

obfuscation._doc: Deterministic. Hidden/non-ASCII characters in tool names (zero-width, homoglyphs).

tool_authz._doc: Deterministic. Tool allowlist with risk levels; unknown tools are denied (fail-closed). action=block on a tool forbids it for agents.

loop_detection._doc: Deterministic. Same tool+args repeated more than N times = runaway agent.

payments._doc: Deterministic business rules for transfer_funds. approval_over = four-eyes threshold.

sql_guard._doc: Deterministic. Blocks destructive and stacked SQL (comments stripped first).

egress._doc: Deterministic. Destinations (email domain / URL host) data may leave to.

secrets._doc: Deterministic. API keys, AWS keys, private keys, password= in inputs (block or redact before the tool sees them) and outputs (always redacted).

pii._doc: Deterministic. email, card_number (Luhn), pesel (checksum), iban. Inputs checked on egress tools only; outputs redacted for redact_output tools, or all tools if output_scope=all.

iban._doc: prompt_action: redact = IBANs in user prompts become a token {{IBAN_n}} plus a masked hint (PL** **** ... 1234); the full value stays in the session vault and is put back only inside resolve_tools, after which the normal payment checks run (beneficiary allowlist, four-eyes, judge). The model never sees the full IBAN. deny = block prompts containing an IBAN.

attack_signatures._doc: Deterministic, externally managed feed of historical AI-infrastructure exploits (file path or http(s) URL, reloaded on change). Calls matching a signature at or above min_severity are blocked.

canary._doc: System-prompt leak detection (OWASP LLM07): the gateway/proxy forwards system prompts via layer.system_prompt_with_canary(), which appends a per-session random token. A model output or tool argument containing it (plain, base64/hex/URL-encoded, spaced or re-cased) is blocked as prompt_leak and taints the session.

semantic._doc: Semantic (AI-based) controls, hybrid and two-tier. A heuristic injection scorer always runs (microseconds). Tier 1 prefilter: small local guard model on every prompt, tool call and tool output. Tier 2 judge: bigger guard model on high_risk_tools or when the prefilter says Controversial. score = max(heuristic, model scores); verdict scores: Unsafe / judge 'yes' = 1.0 (llama-guard: P(unsafe) from logprobs), Controversial = 0.5, Safe = 0. threshold = adherence level: 0.6 balanced (Controversial passes), 0.5 strict. backend: auto (tiers whose model is not pulled are skipped and flagged) | ollama (missing model = failure, fail_mode applies) | heuristic (no models). fail_mode open = continue on heuristic + audit flag semantic=unavailable; closed = prefilter denies, judge requires human approval. on_flag for tool calls: deny (default) | require_approval - a human only via explicit policy rules (four-eyes over payments.approval_over, taint escalation, judge fail_mode closed), never as the default reaction to a guard verdict; a flagged tool output taints the session (on_detect: taint | block). User prompts: prompt_on_detect block | taint; documents (check_prompt direction=document) are always redacted + tainted, never silently passed. An injection hit always taints the session, even when PII in the same text would block it. Only models in models.allowed are used; pinned_digests refuses a model whose Ollama digest changed (supply chain). Circuit breaker: a connection error puts a model on cooldown_s at once; timeouts only after breaker_consecutive_timeouts in a row on inputs <= breaker_short_input_chars (a long input timing out applies fail_mode to that request only, it does not take the model away from other sessions). The next fallback model is tried in the same call. If the prefilter primary failed (degraded:prefilter flag), the judge still runs (judge.escalate_on: controversial | prefilter_failed | heuristic_signal); if the judge then fails too, user prompts stay fail-open (flagged) but phases in degraded_fail_closed_phases fail closed (tool calls require approval, tool outputs and documents are tainted + marked UNTRUSTED). Cold models are warmed at startup and in the background (up to warmup_timeout_ms); the request path never waits longer than the tier timeout; keep_alive keeps models loaded (-1 = never unload; the value sent with each request overrides OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE on the server, so '30m' would unload models after 30 min idle mid-judging). Model tag + digest of every verdict go into the audit record. Verdicts are cached only for a tier's primary model, for cache_ttl_s (0 = off); fallback-model verdicts are never cached; the cache is cleared on every policy change and by POST /admin/cache/clear. Model time counts against budgets.max_compute_ms.

consensus._doc: mode=consensus: every guard below votes IN PARALLEL (Ollama runs different models concurrently: 2 small guards 0.16 s wall, + granite 1.35 s wall = the slowest guard, not the sum). Each vote is normalized to safe / unsafe / unknown (timeout, error, not installed, digest mismatch = unknown, does not vote). Outcome: voters < min_votes -> no quorum (on_no_quorum: heuristic | require_approval | deny); unsafe share >= agreement_threshold -> unsafe (prompts blocked, tool calls per on_flag, outputs taint); safe share >= agreement_threshold -> pass; anything else = disagreement, resolved per tool risk tier (tools.<name>.risk; prompts = prompt_risk, default medium) by on_disagreement (Andrzej, policy owner): arbiter_then_X = ask the arbiter (granite, criterion by phase) and use its verdict; otherwise / if the arbiter is unavailable, a weighted vote with w = log(p/(1-p)) from each guard's measured accuracy (docs/research/swarm-math.md section 5) decides when |sum| >= weighted_margin; still unresolved -> X: allow_flag (ALLOW + guard_disagreement flag in audit/report) or deny (fail-closed). require_approval is available only as an explicit choice, never the default. Accuracy defaults are measured on our small labelled sets (n ~ 10-20): granite 0.9 (w 2.2), qwen3guard 0.85 (w 1.73), llama-guard 0.6 (w 0.41). agreement_threshold 1.0 = unanimity; 0.66 lets 2 of 3 decide. min_confidence per guard: an unsafe verdict below it abstains (unknown) instead of voting - llama-guard3:1b gives false positives at P(unsafe) 0.73-0.82 on legit tool calls (S1) vs 0.977 on real money laundering, so it needs 0.9. Guards are deliberately from different model families (Qwen, Llama, Granite): correlated errors shrink the effective number of independent judges, N_eff = N / (1 + (N - 1) * rho).

judge._doc: granite3.3-guardian criteria are template ids (harm, jailbreak, unethical_behavior, function_call = call/tool-schema hallucination, ...) or free text. Measured on 10 treasury tool calls: unethical_behavior flags the 95k hijack, exfil email, audit-log delete, os.system and an out-of-task 9k payment with 0 false positives on legit calls; harm/jailbreak miss the delete; a custom free-text criterion flagged everything. Ollama serializes calls per model, so each extra criterion adds ~1.3 s warm.
